question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=0,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨1,1,1⟩, \\ N(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(0) & =T(0)\times N(0) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨1,1,1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-1,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨(0-1),-(0-(-1)),(1-(-1))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨-1,-1,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
